Chenaniah
ken-uh-NYE-uh
proper noun
Hebrew Kenanyahu, “the LORD establishes” or “whom the LORD sets up,” the chief Levite for song.

📖 Biblical Definition

Chenaniah was a chief of the Levites in the days of David, set over the song when the ark was brought up to Jerusalem: “Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was for song: he instructed about the song, because he was skilful” (1Ch 15:22). He was the master of the song, who led the singers in the great procession, “Chenaniah the master of the song with the singers” (1Ch 15:27). His office was to teach and order the music of the house of God, that the praise of the LORD might be offered with skill and reverence by trained voices, not in disorder but in beauty and fitness. The Scripture marks that he was appointed to this work because he was skilful; his gift was recognized and set to its proper use in the worship of God. Chenaniah stands as a witness to the place of trained and skilful music in the worship of the LORD, in the line that leads to the great companies of singers Solomon would establish in the temple. He teaches that the praise of God is to be offered with care and excellence; the LORD is worthy of our best, and the gifts He gives are to be cultivated and devoted to His service in the assembly of His people.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A chief Levite set over the song when the ark came to Jerusalem, the skilful master of the music.

CHENANIAH, a chief of the Levites in the days of David.

He was set over the song, and instructed about it, being skilful (1Ch 15:22).

He was the master of the song with the singers (1Ch 15:27).

His office was to teach and order the music of the house of God.

He led the singers when the ark was brought up to Jerusalem.

📖 Key Scripture

1Ch 15:22 — "And Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was for song: he instructed about the song, because he was skilful."

1Ch 15:27 — "And David was clothed with a robe of fine linen, and all the Levites that bare the ark, and the singers, and Chenaniah the master of the song with the singers: David also had upon him an ephod of linen."

1Ch 16:4 — "And he appointed certain of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, and to record, and to thank and praise the LORD God of Israel:"

Ps 33:3 — "Sing unto him a new song; play skilfully with a loud noise."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; he witnesses the place of skilful, reverent music in the worship of God.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the care and excellence due to the praise of God. Chenaniah was set over the song because he was skilful, and he instructed the singers that the worship of the LORD might be offered with beauty and fitness. The praise of God is not to be offered carelessly; the LORD is worthy of our best, and the gifts of music He gives are to be cultivated and devoted to His service.

Chenaniah’s ordered song also stands against both the irreverence that despises beauty in worship and the showmanship that makes worship a performance for men. The aim was the praise of God, offered with skill and reverence by trained Levites under appointed order. True worship is neither slovenly nor self-displaying, but devotes the best of the soul’s gifts to the glory of God in the appointed way.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name means “the LORD establishes,” from Yah (the LORD) and a verb to set up or establish.

expand to see more

Chenaniah — Hebrew Kenanyahu, “the LORD establishes.”

The element Yah is the name of the LORD.

He was a chief of the Levites under David.

He was the skilful master of the song.

He instructed the singers in the worship of God.

Usage

"Like Chenaniah, the worship of God calls for skill and reverence, devoting the best of our gifts."

"Chenaniah teaches that the LORD is worthy of care and excellence in His praise."

"The master of the song shows worship to be neither slovenly nor self-displaying, but ordered to God’s glory."
